arxiv-2012-07573.title: Intersection numbers on ℳ ¯ g , n \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n} and BKP hierarchy
arxiv-2012-07573.creator: Alexander Alexandrov
arxiv-2012-07573.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Alexander Alexandrov. In their recent inspiring paper Mironov and Morozov claim a surprisingly simple expansion formula for the Kontsevich–Witten tau-function in terms of the Schur Q-functions. Here we provide a similar conjecture for the Brézin–Gross–Witten tau-function. Moreover, we identify both tau-functions of the KdV hierarchy, which describe intersection numbers on the moduli spaces of punctured Riemann surfaces, with the hypergeometric solutions of the BKP hierarchy.

arxiv-2102-07724.title: Locality and Centrality: The Variety ZG Thanks: We thank Jean-Éric Pin and Jorge Almeida for their fruitful advice, and thank the anonymous reviewers of ICALP and LMCS for their very helpful feedback.
arxiv-2102-07724.creator: Antoine Amarilli ORCID:0000-0002-7977-4441, Charles Paperman ORCID:0000-0002-6658-5238
arxiv-2102-07724.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Antoine Amarilli ORCID:0000-0002-7977-4441, Charles Paperman ORCID:0000-0002-6658-5238. We study the variety 𝐙𝐆 \mathbf{ZG} of monoids where the elements that belong to a group are central , i.e., commute with all other elements. We show that 𝐙𝐆 \mathbf{ZG} is local , that is, the semidirect product 𝐙𝐆 ∗ 𝐃 \mathbf{ZG}*\mathbf{D} of 𝐙𝐆 \mathbf{ZG} by definite semigroups is equal to 𝐋𝐙𝐆 \mathbf{LZG} , the variety of semigroups where all local monoids are in 𝐙𝐆 \mathbf{ZG} .

arxiv-2202-04674.title: A tale of tails through generalized unitarity
arxiv-2202-04674.creator: Alex Edison, Michèle Levi
arxiv-2202-04674.description: Abstract We introduce a novel framework to study high-order gravitational effects on a binary from the scattering of its emitted gravitational radiation. Here we focus on the radiation-reaction due to the background of the binary’s gravitational potential, namely on the so-called tail effects, as the starting point to this type of scattering effects.

arxiv-2205-04242.title: Explicit Evaluation of Euler-Apéry Type Multiple Zeta Star Values and Multiple t t -Star Values
arxiv-2205-04242.creator: Ce Xu and Jianqiang Zhao[1mm] a. School of Mathematics and Statistics, Anhui Normal University, Wuhu 241002, PRCb. Department of Mathematics, The Bishop’s School, La Jolla, CA 92037, USA
arxiv-2205-04242.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ce Xu and Jianqiang Zhao[1mm] a. School of Mathematics and Statistics, Anhui Normal University, Wuhu 241002, PRCb. Department of Mathematics, The Bishop’s School, La Jolla, CA 92037, USA. In this paper we establish several recurrence relations about Euler-Apéry type multiple zeta star values and a parametric variant of it by using the method of iterated integrals.

arxiv-2305-08683.title: Supersymmetry with Lorentz Symmetry Violation
arxiv-2305-08683.creator: I.T. Drummond
arxiv-2305-08683.description: Abstract We study two (massless free field) models, a photon/photino model with a vector gauge field and a Majorana spinor field, and a Wess-Zumino model. They each exhibit Lorentz symmetry violation but retain, in an appropriate way, the supersymmetry correspondance between the particles of the two fields.

arxiv-2312-10163.title: Towards the Unification of Generative and Discriminative Visual Foundation Model: A Survey
arxiv-2312-10163.creator: Xu Liu, Tong Zhou, Yuanxin Wang, Yuping Wang, Qinjingwen Cao, Weizhi Du, Yonghuan Yang, Junjun He, Yu Qiao, Yiqing Shen
arxiv-2312-10163.description: Abstract The advent of foundation models, which are pre-trained on vast datasets, has ushered in a new era of computer vision, characterized by their robustness and remarkable zero-shot generalization capabilities. Mirroring the transformative impact of foundation models like large language models (LLMs) in natural language processing, visual foundation models (VFMs) have become a catalyst for groundbreaking developments in computer vision.

arxiv-2409-04077.title: Blind-Adaptive Quantizers
arxiv-2409-04077.creator: Aman Rishal Chemmala, Satish Mulleti
arxiv-2409-04077.description: Abstract Sampling and quantization are crucial in digital signal processing, but quantization introduces errors, particularly due to distribution mismatch between input signals and quantizers. Existing methods to reduce this error require precise knowledge of the input’s distribution, which is often unavailable.

arxiv-2501-04780.title: Using quantum nonlocality for device-independent confirmation of relativistic effects
arxiv-2501-04780.creator: Shubhayan Sarkar
arxiv-2501-04780.description: Abstract Synchronizing clocks to measure time is a fundamental process underpinning every practical communication task from GPS to parallel computation. However, as the current protocols are based on classical communication between the sender and receiver, they are prone to simple attacks that could cause a slight delay in the signal which would then cause a massive error in further operations.

arxiv-2501-05725.title: Expanding Molecular Shell and Possible γ \gamma -ray Source Associated with Supernova Remnant Kesteven 67
arxiv-2501-05725.creator: Yun-Zhi Shen (沈蘊之), Yang Chen (陳陽), Xiao Zhang (張瀟), Tian-Yu Tu (涂天宇), Wen-Juan Zhong (鍾文娟) , Qian-Qian Zhang (張芊千) , and Qian-Cheng Liu (劉前程)
arxiv-2501-05725.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yun-Zhi Shen (沈蘊之), Yang Chen (陳陽), Xiao Zhang (張瀟), Tian-Yu Tu (涂天宇), Wen-Juan Zhong (鍾文娟) , Qian-Qian Zhang (張芊千) , and Qian-Cheng Liu (劉前程). We investigate the molecular environment of the supernova remnant (SNR) Kesteven 67 (G18.8+0.3) using observations in 12 CO, 13 CO, HCO + , and HCN lines and possible associated γ \gamma -ray emission using 16-yr Fermi -LAT observation.

arxiv-2507-02388.title: Stringy Corrections to Heterotic SU(3)-Geometry
arxiv-2507-02388.creator: Jock McOrist
arxiv-2507-02388.description: Abstract \proofmodefalse We analyse the {\alpha^{\backprime}\,}^{2} corrections to the supersymmetry algebra constructed by Bergshoeff de Roo for heterotic compactifications on {\rm SU}(3) manifolds. The geometry remains complex, conformally balanced, but H and the hermitian form \omega are corrected to H=i({\partial}-{\overline{\partial}})\omega+{\alpha^{\backprime}\,}P , with P determined in terms of {\text{d}}H .

arxiv-2507-19069.title: Entanglement across scales: Quantics tensor trains as a natural framework for renormalization
arxiv-2507-19069.creator: Stefan Rohshap, Jheng-Wei Li, Alena Lorenz, Serap Hasil, Karsten Held, Anna Kauch, Markus Wallerberger
arxiv-2507-19069.description: Abstract Understanding entanglement remains one of the most intriguing problems in physics. While particle and site entanglement have been studied extensively, the investigation of length or energy scale entanglement — quantifying the information exchange between different length scales — has received far less attention.

arxiv-2512-13506.title: Learning under Distributional Drift: Reproducibility as an Intrinsic Statistical Resource
arxiv-2512-13506.creator: Sofiya C Zaichyk
arxiv-2512-13506.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sofiya C Zaichyk. Statistical learning under distributional drift remains insufficiently characterized: when each observation alters the data-generating law, classical generalization bounds can collapse. We introduce a new statistical primitive, the reproducibility budget C T C_{T} , which quantifies a system’s finite capacity for statistical reproducibility —the extent to which its sampling process can remain governed by a consistent underlying distribution in the presence of both exogenous change and endogenous feedback.

europmc-pmc2570625.title: Hierarchical models in the brain.
europmc-pmc2570625.creator: Friston K.
europmc-pmc2570625.description: This paper describes a general model that subsumes many parametric models for continuous data. The model comprises hidden layers of state-space or dynamic causal models, arranged so that the output of one provides input to another. The ensuing hierarchy furnishes a model for...

pmc-10517967.title: Ultra-durable superhydrophobic cellular coatings
pmc-10517967.creator: Wancheng Gu, Wanbo Li, Yu Zhang, Yage Xia, Qiaoling Wang, Wei Wang, Ping Liu, Xinquan Yu, Hui He, Caihua Liang, Youxue Ban, Changwen Mi, Sha Yang, Wei Liu, Miaomiao Cui, Xu Deng, Zuankai Wang, Youfa Zhang
pmc-10517967.description: Developing versatile, scalable, and durable coatings that resist the accretion of matters (liquid, vapor, and solid phases) in various operating environments is important to industrial applications, yet has proven challenging. Here, we report a cellular coating that imparts liquid-repellence, vapor-imperviousness, and solid-shedding capabilities without the need for complicated structures and fabrication processes.

pmc-11325583.title: Identification of regulatory networks and crosstalk factors in brown adipose tissue and liver of a cold-exposed cardiometabolic mouse model
pmc-11325583.creator: Melina Amor, Malena Diaz, Valentina Bianco, Monika Svecla, Birgit Schwarz, Silvia Rainer, Anita Pirchheim, Laszlo Schooltink, Suravi Mukherjee, Gernot F Grabner, Giangiacomo Beretta, Claudia Lamina, Giuseppe Danilo Norata, Hubert Hackl, Dagmar Kratky
pmc-11325583.description: BackgroundActivation of brown adipose tissue (BAT) has gained attention due to its ability to dissipate energy and counteract cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs).MethodsThis study investigated the consequences of cold exposure on the BAT and liver proteomes of an established CMD mouse model based on LDL receptor-deficient (LdlrKO) mice fed a high-fat, high-sucrose, high-cholesterol diet for 16 weeks.

pmc-11525185.title: Machine-guided design of cell-type-targeting cis-regulatory elements
pmc-11525185.creator: Sager J Gosai, Rodrigo I Castro, Natalia Fuentes, John C Butts, Kousuke Mouri, Michael Alasoadura, Susan Kales, Thanh Thanh L Nguyen, Ramil R Noche, Arya S Rao, Mary T Joy, Pardis C Sabeti, Steven K Reilly, Ryan Tewhey
pmc-11525185.description: Cis-regulatory elements (CREs) control gene expression, orchestrating tissue identity, developmental timing and stimulus responses, which collectively define the thousands of unique cell types in the body1–3. While there is great potential for strategically incorporating CREs in therapeutic or biotechnology applications that require tissue specificity, there is no guarantee that an optimal CRE for these intended purposes has arisen naturally.

pmc-11529992.title: The chromatin tapestry as a framework for neurodevelopment
pmc-11529992.creator: Ben Nolan, Timothy E Reznicek, Christopher T Cummings, M Jordan Rowley
pmc-11529992.description: The neuronal nucleus houses a meticulously organized genome. Within this structure, genetic material is not simply compacted but arranged into a precise and functional 3D chromatin landscape essential for cellular regulation. This mini-review highlights the importance of this chromatin landscape in healthy neurodevelopment, as well as the diseases that occur with aberrant chromatin architecture.

pmc-11588401.title: Des mesures pour éviter les blessures liées aux voiturettes de golf sont requises de toute urgence
pmc-11588401.creator: Douglas Lau, Tara Esbati, Michael D Cusimano
pmc-11588401.description: n plus fréquentes et peuvent être mortelles; les enfants, les personnes âgées et les personnes dont les facultés sont affaiblies par l’alcool ou d’autres substances sont particulièrement vulnérables. La plupart des blessures liées aux voiturettes de golf pourraient être évitées grâce à des dispositifs de sécurité de base comme les ceintures de sécurité et les cages de retournement.

pmc-11679707.title: Impact of Physiotherapy on Shoulder Kinematics in Swimmers with Swimmer’s Shoulder Pain
pmc-11679707.creator: Alessandra Raffini, Miriam Martini, Laura Mazzari, Alex Buoite Stella, Manuela Deodato, Luigi Murena, Agostino Accardo
pmc-11679707.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Swimmer’s shoulder is a common condition among elite swimmers, often leading to pain and reduced performance. Fatigue can exacerbate this condition by affecting shoulder strength, proprioception, and range of motion, potentially increasing the risk of overuse injuries. This preliminary study aimed to evaluate the impact of physiotherapy treatment and the effects of fatigue on shoulder kinematics using inertial and magnetic measurement units (IMUs).

pmc-11790020.title: Live-cell imaging of human liver fibrosis using hepatic micro-organoids
pmc-11790020.creator: Yuan Guan, Zhuoqing Fang, Angelina Hu, Sarah Roberts, Meiyue Wang, Wenlong Ren, Patrik K. Johansson, Sarah C. Heilshorn, Annika Enejder, Gary Peltz
pmc-11790020.description: Due to the limitations of available in vitro systems and animal models, we lack a detailed understanding of the pathogenetic mechanisms of and have minimal treatment options for liver fibrosis. Therefore, we engineered a live-cell imaging system that assessed fibrosis in a human multilineage hepatic organoid in a microwell (i.e., microHOs).

pmc-12683037.title: Valve dehiscence after intra-atrial implantation of mitral prosthesis
pmc-12683037.creator: Shawn M Shah, Gosta B Pettersson, Marc Gillinov, Haytham Elgharably
pmc-12683037.description: n at the right and left trigones,1 which provides an appropriate anchor for durable mitral valve replacement (MVR). Certain pathologies of the mitral annulus pose a challenge to standard MVR, such as radiation-induced heart disease, mitral annular calcification (MAC), invasive endocarditis, or multiple reoperations.

pmc-13374402.title: Occupational therapists’ use of digital technologies to support people with disabilities in engaging in occupation: a scoping review protocol
pmc-13374402.creator: Cheol Jeong, Margaret Jones, Clare Hocking, Christian Krägeloh
pmc-13374402.description: IntroductionDigital tools such as virtual reality, mobile applications and digital devices are being implemented across various healthcare practice settings. Engagement in occupations is central to occupational therapy, supporting health and quality of life. Occupational therapists support people with disabilities to participate in occupations by enhancing their abilities or adapting tasks and environments.

pmc-13417488.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Predictive Nomogram for Assessing Rhabdomyolysis Risk After Wasp Stings: A Multicenter Study in Sichuan, China
pmc-13417488.creator: Xiaoyan Xian, Guoqiang Chen, Jianping Hu, Yuanjun Zhang, Mengqin Li, Jing Chen, Jiao Li, Shuyun Xu, Shashank Kaushik

pmc-13472557.title: Audit and Evaluation of the Effect of Fresh Frozen Plasma and Adjunct Pharmacological Agents (Vitamin K1, Prothrombin Complex Concentrate, Tranexamic Acid, and Recombinant Factor VIIa) on Pre- and Post- Transfusion INR in Patients with Coagulopathy: A Prospective Study
pmc-13472557.creator: Grazy Chinnamuthu, Gowtham Ganapathy, P Padmavathi
pmc-13472557.description: Background:Coagulopathy is frequently encountered in patients with liver disease, trauma, anticoagulant therapy, and perioperative bleeding. Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) is widely used to correct coagulation abnormalities associated with elevated International Normalized Ratio (INR). However, plasma alone may not always provide optimal correction.

pmc-13571278.title: Clinicopathological differences and risk factors of early- versus late-onset pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13571278.creator: Mohammad Alzoubi, Rahaf Al Jibarat, Ahmad Omar Saleh, Reem Eisa, Haneen Mosa Al-sha’ar, Tuqa M Alfreijat, Juman Habboub, Rania Rashed, Rahaf Hanoun, Raghad Alkhateeb, Zaed Hamady
pmc-13571278.description: SummaryPancreatic cancer is one of the most aggressive malignancies worldwide, and the incidence is increasing in patients under the age of 50. We systematically reviewed the clinicopathological features of early-onset pancreatic cancer (EOPC) and late-onset pancreatic cancer (LOPC) to help develop tailored therapeutic strategies and earlier diagnosis for younger patients.

pmc-13586782.title: Eating Behavior, Food Consumption Frequency, and Nutritional Status Among Undergraduate Nursing Students: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13586782.creator: Maria Laura Lacerda Nascimento, Aline Nataly Soares Vital, Taisy Cinthia Ferro Cavalcante, Emily Pereira de Souza, Amanda Alves Marcelino da Silva
pmc-13586782.description: University nursing students face academic and lifestyle pressures that may compromise food choices and nutritional status. This study evaluated the relationship between eating behavior, food consumption frequency, and nutritional status in this population. Cross‐sectional study with 61 undergraduate nursing students. BMI was calculated from measured weight and height (WHO criteria).
